subject: Deployment recommendation & next steps — Stratify pilot
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@stratifyinc.com>, Anya Petrova <anya.p@stratifyinc.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 13:12:00 +0000
Subject: Deployment recommendation & next steps — Stratify pilot

Hi Liam / Anya,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the deep dive into StratoCart (Stratify) checkout flows. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can converge on the right deployment mode.

Call highlights
- Primary ask: persistent, near-real-time personalization calls on checkout (cart total / inventory checks + promo scoring).
- Target SLO: p95 latency target in the 40-80 ms range for the personalization endpoint; bursty traffic during peak sales windows (~250–400 QPS sustained for short periods).
- Data requirements: no PII in requests; preference for US-only residency; SOC2 evidence will be required for procurement.

Initial recommendation (high level)
- We think a two-stage approach will minimize risk: start with Redwood Hosted API for fast time-to-value + an optional Dedicated capacity reservation for production rollouts where predictable throughput and isolation are critical.
  - Hosted gets you running quickly and supports our streaming/kv caching and fallback routing.
  - Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) gives you guaranteed throughput and predictable latency if the p95 constraint hardens.

Attachments: I attached a short latency/traffic sample you sent during the call (stratify_latency_profile.csv) and a one-page pilot outline (attached).

Next steps / asks
1) Confirm whether p95 = enforced SLA (hard) or target (soft).
2) Which endpoints are the highest priority (personalization, promo scoring, fraud detection)?
3) If you prefer Dedicated, we’ll need to confirm residency (US region vs on-prem/VPC).
4) I’ll loop in our solutions engineer (Ben) and infra lead (Priyom) for sizing and a short pilot plan.

Proposed timeline: 2-week pilot (bench + small traffic ramp) -> 4-week production ramp with Dedicated reservation if needed.

Would you like to schedule a 30-min technical follow-up next week? If so, share preferred times and I’ll send invites.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A couple quick clarifications before we lock the follow-up: 

1) The 40-80 ms p95 — that's for the personalization call only. We can tolerate higher for secondary endpoints. Is Hosted able to consistently hit 50 ms p95 for steady-state requests at ~300 QPS? We're wary of tail spikes.

2) If Dedicated is needed, what level of reservation do you recommend to hit that p95 at 300 QPS? Rough sizing is fine — we just need a ballpark to compare to infra budget.

3) Data residency: US-only is required. We may consider a private VPC if procurement requires customer-managed network controls (likely later in the procurement phase).

4) Procurement asks: SOC2 report + retention window options. Our procurement team will need to see SOC2 and a sample data retention policy.

We can do a follow-up next Tue (6/29) afternoon PST. If Hosted is likely to meet the latency target for a pilot, we'd prefer starting there to keep time-to-value short — but we need the sizing numbers and tradeoffs so we can budget.

- Liam

Hi Liam / Anya — Ben here (Solutions Engineer). Thanks for the clear call and the sample profile — that helped. Short, practical recommendation below based on your p95 goal and the traffic profile.

Executive recommendation (pilot -> production)
- Pilot: Start on Redwood Hosted API with a small dedicated reservation for the personalization route (Hybrid approach). Hosted gives fastest rollout and our runtime will use KV/prefix caching to reduce repeated compute for similar carts. The dedicated reservation we recommend during pilot is a single "dedicated slice" (equivalent to ~1-2 A100-class GPUs depending on quantization) to give consistent tail behavior while you validate correctness and integration.

- Production: If p95 at ~300 QPS is a hard SLA, move to Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) sized at ~4 dedicated units (roughly equivalent to 4x baseline A100-class slices) with autoscale headroom for bursts. That configuration has historically given customers <60 ms p95 for dense decoding workloads when we combine KV caching + quantized model variants.

Sourcing the numbers (assumptions)
- Model: 13B dense variant, typical checkout prompt lengths (avg 160 tokens with short response token budgets).
- Quantization: int8 / q4 variants reduce GPU memory and allow more concurrent contexts; we typically see 20–35% latency improvement for tail.
- Caching: prefix + KV cache for repeated cart structures reduces per-request work by ~25–40% depending on cache hit rate.

Operational asks for procurement
- SOC2: we can share our SOC2 Type II report and an annotated data retention + deletion policy (we support configurable retention windows).
- Residency: Hosted supports US-region only; Dedicated can be provisioned in a US-only capacity. If procurement requires customer-managed networking, our Private (VPC) package is the next step — procurement and engineering will need to coordinate for VPC peering and KMS keys.

Pilot plan (proposed)
1) Week 0: Kickoff + integration (API keys, sample traffic)
2) Week 1: Pilot run on Hosted + small dedicated slice, run stress tests to validate p95 and cache behavior
3) Week 2: Review metrics, decide on Dedicated reservation sizing & contract (if SLA required)

Deliverables I can share before Tue call
- Short sizing note (one-pager) and a 2-week pilot runbook (attached: redwood-deploy-plan.pdf).
- SOC2 artifact + retention policy on request (link or NDA-based exchange).

If this sounds good, Marissa can schedule Tue 6/29 2:00–2:30pm PST and we’ll walk through the pilot runbook and sizing note.

Best,
